headline: Funding flows. Satellites surge. Defense budgets rise.
deck: This week saw significant funding and government interest in space resilience and satellite technology.

stories.head: True Anomaly's $190M Series C proves demand
stories.body: True Anomaly raised $190 million in a Series C round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. This funding will bolster its co-orbital security and space domain awareness capabilities, directly addressing the Department of Defense's pressing needs. With the Pentagon increasingly focused on countering threats in orbit, True Anomaly is positioned to capitalize on this trend.
stories.soWhat: It's clear that the military's appetite for space security is only growing, and True Anomaly is right in the crosshairs of that demand.

stories.head: House restores funding for TraCSS, space traffic woes persist
stories.body: The House has reinstated funding for the Traffic Coordination and Safety System (TraCSS), aiming to tackle the anticipated congestion of 7,000+ satellites by the mid-2030s. This legislative move comes as the commercial satellite market expands rapidly, with more players entering the fray. The funding restoration signals a recognition of the complexities involved in space traffic management.
stories.soWhat: If Congress is willing to put money where its mouth is, we might actually see some order in the cosmic chaos.

stories.head: Anduril and L3Harris team up for SDA constellation
stories.body: Anduril and L3Harris have joined forces to bid on a tactical Space Development Agency (SDA) constellation, highlighting a strategic collaboration in the defense sector. This partnership aims to leverage both companies' strengths in advanced technology and defense capabilities. The SDA's push for a more resilient space architecture makes this bid particularly timely.
stories.soWhat: When big players unite, it often means the stakes are high, and the competition is getting serious.

watchlist.title: Monitor TraCSS funding developments

watchlist.body: With fresh capital, True Anomaly's strategic decisions will be critical in shaping its market position.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
